description: Bundles one or more ItemDataTable entries with quantities so shops, progress rewards, mission rewards, and unlock text can grant, spend, price, and display a complete item package as one unit.

Id.technical: FName key used by ShopLineupDataTable::Id_ItemSet, ProgressRewardDataTable::Id_ItemSet, mission/demo reward lists, DLC entitlement lists, and direct shop/ownership lookups. Consumers scan ItemSetDataTables in order and use the first row with the requested name; when no set is found several helpers fall back to probing ItemDataTables with the same ID.

Id_ItemText.simple: Optional override text key for the whole set.
Id_ItemText.technical: FName used by GameShop_GetItemSetNameText after Money and Nickname special cases. When it is None the function falls back to the first contained Item row's Id_ItemText. Every exported row has this field set to None, so the retail snapshot relies on the fallback or the special cases.

Id_Item.simple: Ordered list of ItemDataTable row IDs included in the set.
Id_Item.technical: TArray<FName>. Iterated by grant/spend code, unlock filtering, shop name generation, collection filtering, and DLC entitlement exclusion. None entries are skipped by some loops but are indexed unguarded by others; exported rows use fixed-length arrays with trailing None values. Shop nickname sets rely on indices 0 and 1 being the top/bottom nickname items.

Quantity.simple: Per-item amounts paired element-for-element with Id_Item.
Quantity.technical: TArray<int32>. GameItem_SpendItemSet subtracts Quantity[Index] for each non-None item; GameShop_AddItemSet grants Count * Quantity[Index] (Money via AddUserMoney, others clamped by Item::PossessionMax). Shop item-name requests receive Quantity[Index] as their VALUE parameter; money-set display uses Quantity[0] directly. Mission reward extraction returns ItemSet::Quantity[0] with the first item. Consumers index this array without a length check, so it must stay aligned with Id_Item.

notes: The export contains 2402 rows. Multiple ItemSetDataTable shards can be loaded; helpers take the first matching row and several fall back to an Item row with the same ID, so set IDs and item IDs share a lookup namespace in those call sites.
A set is considered unlocked for display when all non-None named items pass their individual progress gates. Shop and collection code use that test before showing or sorting a set.

The reconstructed GameShop_FindSetRowItem checks the requested index against Id_Item but then reads Id_Item[0] (and applies the first item's progress gate) regardless of Index; this is documented as a retail behavior in the source comment, not a documentation-site inference.
Only the supplied retail export and partial Content are available; no claim is made about all Blueprint or editor-tool uses.

usages.detail: Spends each contained item in the paired quantity.
Grants Count * Quantity of each set item and reports the amounts to KPI/achievement systems.
Builds per-item name text requests using each quantity as the VALUE parameter.
Builds the set title, with Money and Nickname composite special cases.
Treats a set as unlocked only when all named items are unlocked.
Builds nickname archive entries from unlocked sets and sorts them by the first item's SortingOrder.
Adds DLC-entitlement set members to the excluded list for new-item achievement checks.
Extracts the first reward item and its quantity for a story-demo reward display.
